The process can reach the database, and the database is not a restored

post.summary:
Sends a one-time code to an email address or phone number. Answers the
same way whether or not an account exists for it. Codes sent earlier keep
working until they expire, up to the newest few. A code for a phone
number needs `sms_consent`, which is recorded with it: for signing in,
or, from a signed-in account, for checking a number it is adding.

409.description: The phone number replied STOP (`PHONE_OPTED_OUT`)

422.description: Not an email address or phone number (`INVALID_IDENTIFIER`), a phone number of a country the service does not take (`PHONE_COUNTRY_NOT_SERVED`), a phone number without `sms_consent`, or with wording that is not the current one (`SMS_CONSENT_REQUIRED`), or a consent in a language not supported (`INVALID_REQUEST`)

429.description: Too many codes requested for this identifier or from this address (`TOO_MANY_REQUESTS`), or too many wrong codes for this identifier today, so none is sent (`TOO_MANY_GUESSES`)

delete.summary: Signs out: the session stops working everywhere it was held.

post.summary: Signs in with a one-time code, creating the account on first use.

401.description: The code is wrong, expired or used up

Blocks the other party of this exchange. Neither of the two can then join
an exchange the other starts. Whatever is waiting to be signed between
them is withdrawn or declined; an agreement in force stays in force. The
other party is not told.

Does one thing to an exchange: accept, decline or withdraw a revision,
act on a contribution, confirm or reject whoever claimed the invitation,
discard a draft, or end or close it.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique per attempt to make this change

200.description: Done; the exchange as it now stands

403.description: That is for the other party to do

get.summary:
What has happened in an exchange, oldest first, with what the parties
wrote along the way: the message sent with a revision, a note on a claim,
the reason for a dispute, a statement. Answers with the latest events, 50
unless `limit` says otherwise and never more than 200; `earlier` in the
answer is the `before` that reads the page before.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Return events before this sequence number. Leave out for the latest.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many events to return: 50 unless said, 200 at most.

404.description: No such exchange for this account

422.description: The query is not valid

200.description: The new link token, shown once

409.description: Someone is in the invited party's place

422.description: Neither or both of `bound_to` and `for_anyone: true`

post.summary:
Records that the initiator opened a way to pass the invitation link on:
the share sheet, a text message, an email, WhatsApp, a copy or its QR
code. Yuppers never sends the link itself, so this is all the service can
know about whether it went anywhere, and it says only that the sender
opened a way to send it, not that it arrived. Shown back as
`invitation_shared_at` on the exchange and in the list. Harmless to
repeat: the latest time is kept. A claim counts as a share when none was
recorded, so a claimed link always has a time.

403.description: Only the initiator has a link to send

404.description: No such exchange for this account

409.description: Someone is in the invited party's place, or the exchange is not open

post.summary:
Gives up the invited party's place. For someone who opened an invitation
link and has not been confirmed by the initiator: it is their way out,
since they cannot decline. Anything they signed is void, and from then on
the exchange does not exist for them.

403.description: The initiator cannot leave their own exchange

404.description: No such exchange for this account

409.description: The caller has been confirmed, and is a party for good

put.summary:
Shows the signed-in party's payment options to the other party of this
agreement, or stops. Not part of the terms: it changes no version, is
not signed and is not in the history. The other party sees them only
while they owe money on the agreement in force that is still to be paid.

404.description: No such exchange, or the caller is not a party to it

409.description: To turn them on: the agreement is a draft or closed, or the account has no payment options saved (`ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`). Turning them off always works

429.description: Too many changes to payment options this hour

get.summary:
The record of an exchange as one self-contained document, for a party to
keep or hand to someone else: how it stands, every revision sent with
what it says and what became of it, every signature and what it rests
on, and everything that happened, in order.
get.description:
One document holds at most 500 events, and at most 50 revisions or about
a megabyte of their text, whichever comes first. A longer record
continues in further documents: `part.next` holds the two values to ask
for the next one with, and `part.complete` says when one document is all
of it.

parameters.name: revisions_after
parameters.description:
Continue after the revision with this sequence number. Taken from
`part.next` of the part before.

parameters.name: events_after
parameters.description:
Continue after the event with this sequence number. Taken from
`part.next` of the part before.

200.description: The record, or one part of it

404.description: No such exchange for this account

422.description: The query is not valid

post.summary:
Reports an exchange, and with it the other party, for review. The other
party is not told. Reporting the same exchange again while the first
report is open changes nothing and is answered the same way.

404.description: No such exchange for this account

409.description: Nobody has joined the exchange yet

422.description: Details too long, or missing for `OTHER`

429.description: Too many reports today

post.summary:
Sends a revision, which signs it: a first proposal, a counteroffer, or an
amendment to an agreement in force. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header so a
retry cannot send it twice.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique per attempt to make this change

404.description: No such exchange for this account

409.description: Refused by the rules, or the exchange changed

422.description: The revision is not valid

get.summary: Where the signed-in party stands on text updates for this agreement.

404.description: No such exchange, or the caller is not a party to it

put.summary:
Turns text updates for this agreement on or off. Turning them on records
the consent (the account, the agreement, the number, the time, the
wording's version and language, the client, and the request's address
and user agent) and queues a confirmation text; turning them off is
recorded too. Repeating either changes nothing.

404.description: No such exchange, or the caller is not a party to it

409.description: The agreement is a draft or closed, or the account has no phone number (`ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`); the wording shown is not the current one (`CONSENT_OUTDATED`); the number replied STOP (`PHONE_OPTED_OUT`)

422.description: No consent given, or a language not supported (`INVALID_REQUEST`); a number of a country not texted (`PHONE_COUNTRY_NOT_SERVED`)

503.description: Text messages are not sent here

post.summary:
Adds the caller's pass to Apple Wallet: the signed `.pkpass`. A party to
the exchange only, and only once something is agreed.

404.description: No such exchange for this account, or Apple Wallet passes are not available (WALLET_UNAVAILABLE)

409.description: Nothing has been agreed yet

429.description: Asked for too often

post.summary:
A link that downloads the caller's Apple pass once, for a few minutes,
without a session: opened in Safari, it adds the pass to Wallet. For the app and
the web page, which hold the session themselves.

404.description: No such exchange for this account, or Apple Wallet passes are not available (WALLET_UNAVAILABLE)

409.description: Nothing has been agreed yet

429.description: Asked for too often

post.summary:
The "Save to Google Wallet" link for the caller's pass. A party to the
exchange only, and only once something is agreed.

404.description: No such exchange for this account, or Google Wallet passes are not available (WALLET_UNAVAILABLE)

409.description: Nothing has been agreed yet

429.description: Asked for too often

post.summary:
Adds to the signed-in account the email address or phone number an
invitation was sent to, with the code sent there, and opens the
invitation: the account takes the invited party's place, as named, so
nobody has to confirm it. Both happen, or neither does. If the address
belongs to another account the answer is `IDENTIFIER_ON_OTHER_ACCOUNT`
with the offer to combine the two; once combined, claiming the
invitation (`POST /v1/invitations/claim`) opens it.

401.description: Not signed in, or the code is wrong

403.description: The invitation was made before its address was kept (`INVITATION_NOT_FOR_YOU`)

404.description: The link is not valid, or no longer

409.description: The address is another account's (`IDENTIFIER_ON_OTHER_ACCOUNT`, with `combine`); the account has another of this kind and `replace` was not given (`IDENTIFIER_KIND_TAKEN`), or no good `proof` (`PROOF_REQUIRED`, `IDENTIFIER_TOO_RECENT`); or the two accounts cannot be combined

422.description: Not the address the invitation was sent to (`NOT_INVITED_ADDRESS`)

429.description: Too many wrong codes or attempts

503.description: A code sent by text could not be checked

post.summary:
Sends a one-time code to the email address or phone number an invitation
was sent to, for someone signed in with another who wants to add it to
their account and open the invitation (`sent_to` in its preview). The
person types the address; unless it is the one the invitation was sent
to, nothing is sent and the answer is `NOT_INVITED_ADDRESS`, which says
nothing more. Requests are counted by account and by invitation
(`TOO_MANY_REQUESTS`), besides the usual limits on codes.

403.description: The invitation was made before its address was kept: only that address can open it (`INVITATION_NOT_FOR_YOU`)

404.description: The link is not valid, or no longer (`INVITATION_UNAVAILABLE`)

409.description: The invitation names nobody, or this account already (`ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`), or no code could be sent there (`CODE_NOT_SENT`)

422.description: Not the address the invitation was sent to (`NOT_INVITED_ADDRESS`), not an address at all (`INVALID_IDENTIFIER`), a phone number without `sms_consent` (`SMS_CONSENT_REQUIRED`), or of a country not served (`PHONE_COUNTRY_NOT_SERVED`)

429.description: Too many codes or attempts asked for

post.summary:
Takes the invited party's place in the exchange. With `only_if_yours`,
only opens it for the account that already took that place.

200.description: Claimed; the exchange as the new party sees it

404.description: The link is not valid, or no longer

post.summary:
Shows the proposal behind an invitation link, to someone signed in. The
token travels in the body so it never appears in a URL the service logs.
post.description:
Without a session the answer is `UNAUTHENTICATED` whatever the token, so
nobody signed out learns anything about any link (DESIGN.md §9): the only
answers about a link come from an account, and an account that is blocked
gets the dead-link answer.

401.description: Not signed in, whatever the token

404.description: The link is not valid, or no longer

post.summary:
Reports the proposal behind an invitation link, and with it the person
who sent it. Like reading the proposal, it needs a session: signed out,
the answer is `UNAUTHENTICATED` whatever the token, so a report cannot be
used to test a link either (DESIGN.md §9). The token is the proof of
having received the proposal and travels in the body, as for the preview.
A link that shows this account no preview takes no report from it.

401.description: Not signed in, whatever the token

404.description: The link is not valid, or no longer

409.description: The link is the caller's own

422.description: Details too long, or missing for `OTHER`

429.description: Too many reports today

patch.summary: Changes the display name or language, or records that the holder is an adult.

422.description: Invalid request

post.summary:
Combines into the signed-in account the account an offer names. It
cannot be undone: that account's place in each of its yups, the address
or number proved and what else the offer lists move here, and it can no
longer be signed in to. Where it replaces this account's own address or
number, it needs `proof`. Every email address either account had is
told; with none, the app shows a notice. The offer is good once, for ten
minutes, from this account only; a repeat with the same
`Idempotency-Key` succeeds and changes nothing.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique per attempt to make this change

200.description: Combined; the account as it now is

409.description: The offer is used, expired or no longer true (`COMBINE_EXPIRED`), the two cannot be combined (`COMBINE_SUSPENDED`, `COMBINE_REVIEWER`, `COMBINE_SHARED_EXCHANGE`), or the offer needs a proof and none good was given (`PROOF_REQUIRED`)

503.description: The accounts were busy and nothing was done; try again

get.summary: What deleting the account would do to the exchanges it is in. Changes nothing.

post.summary:
Deletes the signed-in account. Every session ends, its email address and
phone number are released, its working data is removed, and each exchange
it is still in is ended or put on the way to closing. Agreements the
other party signed stay in that party's record. It cannot be undone.

401.description: Not signed in, or the code is wrong, expired, used up or was sent for something else

422.description: The account has no such identifier

429.description: Too many wrong deletion codes from this account today

503.description: The account was busy and nothing was done, or a code sent by text could not be checked because the provider that made it did not answer; the code still works

post.summary:
Sends a one-time code for deleting the account to its own email address
or phone number. The code is good for that and nothing else. Requests are
counted against the account, apart from sign-in codes, so nobody asking
for sign-in codes for the same address can use them up. A code by text
needs `sms_consent`, which is recorded with it.

409.description: The phone number replied STOP (`PHONE_OPTED_OUT`)

422.description: The account has no such identifier, or a consent in a language not supported (`INVALID_REQUEST`); its phone number is of a country the service does not take (`PHONE_COUNTRY_NOT_SERVED`); or `PHONE` without `sms_consent`, or with wording that is not the current one (`SMS_CONSENT_REQUIRED`)

429.description: Too many deletion codes requested by this account

put.summary:
Registers this device for push notifications, under the session making
the request, or updates it if it is registered already.
put.description:
A token is one device, and it moves to this session only if it is not
registered, is registered by the same account, or is registered under a
session that has ended (signed out, revoked or expired): the same phone
signed into another account afterwards. Registered under another
account's live session, it stays where it is, so that someone who has
learned a token cannot take another person's notifications. That is
answered exactly as a registration is, with the device's ID, which this
account cannot use; a different answer would say that the token belongs
to someone. The cost falls on a phone handed on without signing out: it
is notified for the old account until that session ends (at most the
session's lifetime), and the app's next registration after that takes it.

200.description: The device, registered (or, if another account's live session holds the token, left as it was and answered the same)

422.description: Not an Expo push token, a platform, a version or a language

delete.summary:
Stops sending push notifications to a device of the caller's. Answers
the same whether or not there was such a device, so a request repeated,
or one about a device already removed, is fine.

post.summary:
Verifies an email address or phone number and attaches it to the
account, with a proof of one it already has (`proof`): adding one, or
replacing the one of the same kind. A proof from an identifier that came
in the last 24 hours does not replace an older one. The address replaced
is told by email; a number replaced, by a notice in the app. An account
with both a verified email and a verified phone can meet the higher risk
tier. If the code is right and the identifier belongs to another
account, the answer is `IDENTIFIER_ON_OTHER_ACCOUNT` with an offer to
combine the two (`POST /v1/me/combine`); until the code is right, an
identifier with an account is answered like any other.

401.description: Not signed in, or the code is wrong

409.description: The identifier belongs to another account, which the code shows the person controls (`IDENTIFIER_ON_OTHER_ACCOUNT`, with `combine`), or that account cannot be combined into this one (`COMBINE_SUSPENDED`, `COMBINE_REVIEWER`, `COMBINE_SHARED_EXCHANGE`); or the account has an identifier and no good `proof` was given (`PROOF_REQUIRED`), or one from an identifier too new to replace an older one (`IDENTIFIER_TOO_RECENT`)

422.description: Not an email address or phone number (`INVALID_IDENTIFIER`), or a phone number of a country the service does not take (`PHONE_COUNTRY_NOT_SERVED`)

429.description: Too many wrong codes for this identifier today (`TOO_MANY_GUESSES`), or a wrong code from an address that has offered too many this hour (`TOO_MANY_REQUESTS`)

503.description: A code sent by text could not be checked, because the provider that made it did not answer; nothing was counted

post.summary:
Proves, with a code sent to one of the account's own identifiers, that
the person signed in controls it: what adding or replacing an email
address or phone number needs, directly, from an invitation, or by
combining another account into this one (`proof`). Good once, for ten
minutes, for this account only, and only while the account still has
the identifier proved.

401.description: Not signed in, or the code is wrong, expired or used up

422.description: The account has no such identifier

429.description: Too many wrong codes for that identifier today

503.description: A code sent by text could not be checked; nothing was counted

delete.summary:
Removes the account's email address or phone number, keeping the other:
an account keeps one to sign in with (`LAST_IDENTIFIER`). Proved with a
code sent to the one that stays, so that a session alone cannot take a
way in away, and the person knows they can still sign in; a code to one
that came in the last 24 hours does not remove one the account had
before it (`IDENTIFIER_TOO_RECENT`). An email
address removed is told by email; a phone number removed, by a notice in
the app. Removing the phone number ends text updates for every
agreement. Invitations named for the address or number removed are left
as they are. Removing one the account does not have changes nothing and
succeeds, as a repeat finds; so does a repeat with the same
`Idempotency-Key`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique per attempt to make this change

401.description: Not signed in, or the code is wrong, expired or used up

409.description: It is the account's only identifier (`LAST_IDENTIFIER`), or the one that stays came in the last 24 hours and the one removed is older (`IDENTIFIER_TOO_RECENT`)

429.description: Too many wrong codes for the identifier that stays today

503.description: A code sent by text could not be checked; nothing was counted

200.description: What is saved; each absent one is null

put.summary:
Saves the account's payment options, replacing what was saved: one left
out or empty is removed. With none left, they stop being shown on every
agreement.

200.description: What is now saved, as stored

422.description: One of them is not a username, $Cashtag, PayPal.Me name, or email address or US phone number for Zelle

429.description: Too many changes to payment options this hour

delete.summary:
Removes all of the account's payment options, and stops showing them on
every agreement.

429.description: Too many changes to payment options this hour

put.summary:
Saves one of the account's payment options, adding it or changing it,
and leaves the others as they are. It is marked changed only if its
value is new, so the payer's warning beside it stays true.

200.description: What is now saved, all of them, as stored

404.description: No such kind of payment option

422.description: Not a username, $Cashtag, PayPal.Me name, or email address or US phone number for Zelle; empty is not one either (remove it instead)

429.description: Too many changes to payment options this hour

delete.summary:
Removes one of the account's payment options, leaving the others as they
are. Removing the last one stops showing them on every agreement, as
removing them all does. Removing one not saved changes nothing.

200.description: What is still saved, as stored

404.description: No such kind of payment option

429.description: Too many changes to payment options this hour

get.summary: Identifies the service and its build, and says how old a client may be.

post.summary:
Twilio's webhook for a text sent to our number. Refused with 403, and
nothing read, unless `X-Twilio-Signature` is Twilio's signature, under
the account's auth token, of this URL as Twilio requested it (the web
origin and this path) and the posted parameters; refused with 413 when
the body is larger than 32 KB (`INBOUND_BODY_LIMIT`) or carries more
than a hundred parameters. A stop keyword puts the number on the opt-out list
and turns off every agreement's updates to it; a start keyword takes it
off the list. A message already taken (by its `MessageSid`) changes
nothing again, so a request posted twice, or replayed, is answered the
same but does nothing. Answered at once, with an empty TwiML document:
Twilio's Advanced Opt-Out sends the replies.

requestBody.description: Twilio's parameters for a message received: From, Body, OptOutType and the rest

403.description: Not signed by Twilio, or no auth token to check it with

413.description: Too large, or too many parameters, to be Twilio's

get.summary:
Staff only. Content hidden by review, most recently hidden first,
leaving out what is hidden from the reviewer and what a report they take
part in hid. Limited per reviewer, with the other lists.

401.description: The reviewer must sign in again (`SESSION_TOO_OLD`)

404.description: Not a reviewer

429.description: Too many lists read in the last hour

post.summary:
Staff only. Shows hidden content to the account again. A note is
required. Content hidden from the reviewer, or by a report they take part
in, is "not found".

401.description: The reviewer must sign in again (`SESSION_TOO_OLD`)

404.description: Not a reviewer, or nothing hidden there

422.description: The note is missing or too long

429.description: Too many actions in the last hour

get.summary:
Staff only. The open reports, oldest first, each with its age, its
reason and its exchange's code, and nothing of what the reporter wrote or
who they are: those are read by opening the report. Reports the reviewer
takes part in are left out. Limited per reviewer, with the other lists.

401.description: The reviewer must sign in again (`SESSION_TOO_OLD`)

404.description: Not a reviewer

429.description: Too many lists read in the last hour

get.summary:
Staff only. Opens an open report: what it says, who it is about, the
reported exchange's record with nothing hidden, and what review has done
so far. Recorded in the audit history. A resolved report shows nothing
more. A report the reviewer takes part in (they made it, it is about
them, or they hold or held a place in its exchange) is "not found".

401.description: The reviewer must sign in again (`SESSION_TOO_OLD`)

404.description: Not a reviewer, or no such report

409.description: Already resolved (`REPORT_RESOLVED`)

429.description: Too many reports opened in the last hour

post.summary:
Staff only. Resolves an open report, once: dismissed, the exchange's
content hidden from the person reported, their account suspended, or
both. A note is required for every outcome but `DISMISSED`. A report the
reviewer takes part in is "not found"; suspending another reviewer is
refused (`SUBJECT_IS_REVIEWER`).

401.description: The reviewer must sign in again (`SESSION_TOO_OLD`)

404.description: Not a reviewer, or no such report

409.description: Already resolved (`REPORT_RESOLVED`), the outcome cannot apply (`ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`), or the person reported is a reviewer, whom only the owner can suspend (`SUBJECT_IS_REVIEWER`)

422.description: The note is missing or too long

429.description: Too many actions in the last hour

get.summary:
Staff only. The suspended accounts, most recently suspended first,
leaving out the reviewer's own and those a report they take part in led
to. Limited per reviewer, with the other lists.

401.description: The reviewer must sign in again (`SESSION_TOO_OLD`)

404.description: Not a reviewer

429.description: Too many lists read in the last hour

post.summary:
Staff only. Lifts a suspension; the account can sign in again. A note is
required. The reviewer's own suspension, and one that a report they take
part in led to, is "not found"; a reviewer's is the owner's to lift
(`SUBJECT_IS_REVIEWER`).

401.description: The reviewer must sign in again (`SESSION_TOO_OLD`)

404.description: Not a reviewer, or no such suspended account

409.description: The account is a reviewer's (`SUBJECT_IS_REVIEWER`)

422.description: The note is missing or too long

429.description: Too many actions in the last hour

adult_confirmed.description: The holder has confirmed they are 18 or over. Required before signing.

display_name.description: Empty until the person has chosen one.

language.description: A supported language tag, such as `en` or `es`.

oneOf.description:
Something that happened to the account with no email address to tell
about it: the clients show it once, until it is dismissed
(`dismiss_notice` in `PATCH /v1/me`). Absent otherwise.

terms_accepted_at.description: When it was accepted, as RFC 3339.

terms_version.description:
The version of the Terms and the Privacy policy accepted at the
latest sign-in (`TERMS_VERSION`). Absent until the account signs in
again after this was first recorded. Only the account's own.

AccountNotice.description: A notice the app shows once on the account.

AccountProof.description:
A proof that the person signed in controls one of the account's own
identifiers, from a code sent to it: what replacing an identifier needs.

proof.description: Good once, for ten minutes, for this account only.

Actor.description:
Who did something: one of the two parties, or the service acting on a
timer.

code.description: The one-time code sent to it.

identifier.description:
An email address, or a phone number: in international form, or a US
number without its country code as people there write it, ten digits
or 1 and ten (`(856) 548-8780`), which is taken as `+1`.

proof.description:
While the account has an identifier, of either kind: a proof of one
it has (`POST /v1/me/identifiers/proof`). Without a good one the
request is refused with `PROOF_REQUIRED` (or `IDENTIFIER_TOO_RECENT`),
before the code is looked at.

code.description: The code sent to the address the invitation was sent to.

identifier.description: The address the code was sent to, as typed for it.

proof.description:
A proof of one of the account's own identifiers
(`POST /v1/me/identifiers/proof`): adding one takes it. Without a
good one the request is refused, before the code is looked at, with
`PROOF_REQUIRED` (or `IDENTIFIER_TOO_RECENT`).

replace.description:
The account has another address of this kind (`sent_to.replaces`):
`true` replaces it. Without it such a request is refused, before the
code is looked at, with `IDENTIFIER_KIND_TAKEN`.

BlockStatus.description:
Whether the caller has blocked the other party of an exchange. Says
nothing about whether the other party has blocked the caller.

name.description:
The other party's name as the exchange writes it. An exchange closed
before anything was agreed shows no terms to read it from.

BlockedPerson.description:
Someone the caller has blocked, named as an exchange the two share names
them. The exchange is also how to unblock them.

left.description:
Set when the caller is no longer in that exchange and cannot open it:
they had opened its invitation and left before being confirmed. It
still names the person, and unblocking through it still works.

name.description: Their name as written in that exchange.

BoundAddress.description:
Whom an invitation names, as someone signed in with another address is
told it: the kind alone.

replaces.description:
The account already has another address of this kind: adding this
one replaces it, which needs `replace: true` and a proof of one of
the account's own (`POST /v1/me/identifiers/proof`).

only_if_yours.description:
Only open the exchange if the signed-in account already holds the
place this link gave, and never take it: anything else, a live link
included, is answered `INVITATION_UNAVAILABLE`. For a client that
finds a link spent and wants to take the person who used it back to
their exchange without claiming anything they did not tap for.

Claimant.description: Who claimed the invitation, shown to the initiator so they can confirm.

CodeChannel.description: Which of the account's identifiers a code is sent to.

proof.description:
Where the offer says `proof_required`: a proof of one of this
account's own identifiers (`POST /v1/me/identifiers/proof`).

token.description:
The token of the offer: `combine.token` in an
`IDENTIFIER_ON_OTHER_ACCOUNT` answer.

CombineOffer.description:
What combining another account into this one would do, and the token
that does it (`POST /v1/me/combine`). It cannot be undone.

payment_options_move.description:
The other account's payment options become this one's, because this
one has none. With options of its own, the other's are dropped.

proof_required.description:
This account's own identifier of the kind proved would be replaced:
combining then needs a proof of one of its own
(`POST /v1/me/identifiers/proof`), as replacing it directly does.

proved.description: The kind of identifier proved, which comes to this account.

text_updates_end.description: The other account's text updates end, because its number is dropped.

token.description: Good once, for [`OFFER_TTL`], from this account only.

CombineOffered.description:
The answer when an address proved belongs to another account: the
refusal's code, `IDENTIFIER_ON_OTHER_ACCOUNT`, and the offer.

oneOf.description: Sign the open revision.
Take back a revision you sent, before it takes effect.

Throw away a draft that was never sent. It closes with nothing agreed
and leaves the list. Only the initiator has one, and only until the
first revision is sent.

Claim, confirm, dispute or waive a contribution. A dispute needs a
reason, and a claim after a dispute needs a note.
The initiator confirms who claimed the invitation.

The initiator says whoever claimed the invitation is not who they
invited. That person is removed, anything they signed is void, and a
new invitation link can be issued.

Consent.description:
Which consent wording the signer was shown. Signing is refused unless it
is the current version.

language.description: The language the wording was shown in, as a supported language tag.

ConsentShown.description: Which consent wording the signer was shown before signing.

Continuation.description: Where to continue reading a record too long for one document.

amount_minor.description: Whole minor units of the exchange's currency. Money only.

id.description:
Chosen by the client for a new contribution; kept unchanged for one
carried over from an earlier revision.

ContributionRef.description:
A contribution, with its description as the parties wrote it in the
revision the event happened under.

since.description:
When it came to stand this way, RFC 3339. Not sent where it is not
known, such as on an agreement coming into force in the history.

started_from.description:
How the author began: a template and its version (`job-deposit-balance@1`),
`blank` or `copy`. Kept once for aggregate counts; never returned.
Clients that send nothing leave it unset.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name, such as `America/Chicago`. Due dates are read in it.

code.description: The one-time code sent to the identifier.

language.description:
The language the client is showing, as a tag such as `es-MX`. Used only
when this creates the account; an unsupported one becomes the default.

terms_version.description:
The version of the Terms and the Privacy policy the client showed
above the button (`TERMS_VERSION`); signing in is the assent to both.
A version the service does not know is refused. Absent from builds
that predate it: the sign-in completes and nothing is recorded.

code.description: The one-time code sent for deleting the account.

DeletionPreview.description:
What deleting the account would do to the exchanges it is in, counted, so
that the person can be told before they confirm.

agreements_in_force.description: Agreements in force. Each gets a request to close, in the account's name.

drafts.description: Drafts never sent. They are discarded.

open_proposals.description: Negotiations with an offer on the table. They end with nothing agreed.

Delivery.description: How the client wants to hold the session.

id.description: The device's ID, for removing it again.

oneOf.description: A calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the exchange's timezone.
When the agreement is accepted.
When another contribution in the same revision is accepted.

ErrorCode.description:
Stable codes for every refusal the API can return. Clients map these to
wording in the user's language and never parse message text
(DESIGN.md §13.3). Adding a code here is a contract change: the generated
client makes the shared wording tables fail to compile until it is covered.

EventType.description:
Everything that can happen to an exchange. Events of any other kind are
not part of what the parties are shown.

counterparty.description:
Who is in the invited party's place, as on the exchange's view, so
the initiator's list can say that nobody has joined yet.

invitation_shared_at.description:
As on the exchange's view: only for the initiator while nobody is in
the invited party's place, when they last opened a way to pass the
link on, if they have.

close_request_lapses_at.description:
When the close request's response window runs out and the exchange
closes unresolved, unless the request is taken back or what is
outstanding is resolved first (DESIGN.md §5.3). RFC 3339. Computed
here, so every client shows the same moment.

content_hidden.description:
A reviewer has hidden what the parties wrote in this exchange from
the viewer (DESIGN.md §9): the terms, the descriptions, the criteria
and the messages read as one placeholder in the viewer's language,
there is no working copy, and signing or sending terms is refused
with `CONTENT_HIDDEN`. Always sent; a client may read its absence as
`false`.

contributions.description: Status of each contribution in the agreement in force.

display_code.description: For telling exchanges apart. Not a credential.

draft.description: The viewer's own unsent working copy.

oneOf.description: The agreement currently binding, if any.

invitation_open.description:
Only for the initiator, and only while nobody is in the invited
party's place: whether an invitation link is out that can still be
used. It is not once the link has been used, even by someone since
removed, or has expired; a new one has to be issued.

invitation_shared_at.description:
With `invitation_open`: when the initiator last opened a way to pass
the link on (RFC 3339), such as a text message or the share sheet,
as the apps report it (`POST /v1/exchanges/{id}/invitation/shared`).
Yuppers never sends the link itself, so this says the sender opened a
way to send it, not that it arrived. Null until they have, and for a
link that replaced an earlier one until that one is shared too.

oneOf.description: The revision awaiting acceptance, if any.

other_party_left.description:
The other party has deleted their account and can no longer act in
this exchange. Said only while the exchange is still open, which is
when the viewer needs to know it. Always sent; a client may read its
absence as `false`.

payment_options.description:
Payment options on this agreement (`crate::payments`): whether the
viewer shows theirs, and the other party's where the viewer may see
them. Not part of the terms. Always sent; a client may read its
absence as nothing shown either way.

version.description: Send this back as `expected_version` with the next change.

name.description: Their name as the exchange writes it.

HistoryPage.description: A stretch of an exchange's history, oldest first.

content_hidden.description:
A reviewer has hidden what the parties wrote in this exchange from
the reader: every note in this page reads as the same placeholder, in
the reader's language (DESIGN.md §9). Always sent; a client may read
its absence as `false`.

earlier.description:
Set when there is history before this page: pass it as `before` to
read the page before.

IdentifierKind.description: A kind of identifier, as the API names it.

IdentifierOutcome.description:
What becomes of each kind of identifier when the two are combined, from
the point of view of the account that stays.

InAppNotice.description:
A notice the app shows once on the account, where there is no email
address to tell (`account.notice_kind`).

identifier.description:
The email address or phone number the person says the invitation was
sent to, typed in full.

oneOf.description:
For a phone number, required: the box beside it was ticked
(`smsCode.verifyNumber`), with the version and language of the
wording shown. Ignored for an email address.

InvitationOptions.description:
Who an invitation link is for, said outright: one of `bound_to` and
`for_anyone: true`, never both and never neither. A link anyone holding
it can claim is never what a request gets by leaving something out.

bound_to.description:
Names who the invitation is for: only an account that has verified
this email address or phone number can claim it. A phone number is
read as signing in reads it: a US number may leave out the `+1`.

for_anyone.description:
`true` for a link anyone who has it can claim. Required, as `true`,
when `bound_to` is not given.

InvitationPreview.description: What someone holding an invitation link sees before signing in.

bound.description: The invitation names a specific person.

currency.description: The exchange's currency, which its amounts are in.

oneOf.description:
Present when the invitation names an email address or phone number
the signed-in account does not have: only which kind, never the
address, in full or masked. Someone who knows it can type it, and
with a code sent there add it to their account and open the
invitation (`POST /v1/invitations/address/codes`); claiming it as it
is is refused with `INVITATION_NOT_FOR_YOU`.

timezone.description: The exchange's IANA timezone, which its due dates are read in.

built_at.description:
When the running build was made, as an RFC 3339 time in UTC; null
when the build did not say.

code_sender.description:
The email address sign-in codes come from, such as
`no-reply@yuppers.app`: the address part of `EMAIL_FROM` (or
`SMTP_FROM`), without its display name, whether codes go by Resend or
SMTP. A client tells someone waiting for a code to look for
it, in their spam folder too. Absent where codes are not sent by
email from an address of the service's own (the development log).

commit.description:
The git commit the running build was made from, in full, or
`unknown` when the build did not say. Also in every response's
`X-Yuppers-Version` header, shortened to seven characters.

minimum_client_versions.description:
The oldest build of each client that may still change anything. A
client below its minimum shows that it must be updated; its changes
are refused with `CLIENT_TOO_OLD`. Absent for a client with no minimum.

push_notifications.description:
Whether the service sends push notifications. An app offers them, and
registers its device (`PUT /v1/me/devices`), only when it does.

sign_in_channels.description:
The kinds of identifier this deployment can send a one-time code to
right now, email first: `email` while codes go by email (or to the
development log), `phone` while text messages are sent (or, in
development, phone codes go to the log too). A client asks only for
these when someone signs in or adds an identifier; a code for any
other kind is refused with `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`.

sms_country_codes.description:
The country calling codes, such as `+1`, of the phone numbers codes
can be sent to (`PHONE_COUNTRY_NOT_SERVED` refuses any other). Empty
when `sign_in_channels` has no `phone`.

sms_updates.description:
Whether a party may turn on text updates for an agreement
(`GET`/`PUT /v1/exchanges/{id}/sms-updates`): while text messages are
sent. A client shows no "Text updates" control otherwise.

wallet_platforms.description:
The wallets a pass can be added to here (DESIGN.md §11). Empty until
a deployment configures one; a client shows no Wallet button then.

MinimumClientVersions.description:
The oldest version of each client that may still change anything.
`None` means every version may.

NewInvitationReport.description:
A report on the proposal behind an invitation link, from someone signed
in who holds the link. The token is their proof of having received it.

details.description: As for a report on an exchange.

What the reporter wants a reviewer to know. Optional, except with the
reason `OTHER`. At most 2,000 characters.

Notices.description: What a reader of the document needs to be told, in its language.

content_hash.description: How to recompute a content hash.

signatures.description: What a signature here rests on.

statements.description: That what the parties recorded about delivery is theirs alone.

OpenedReport.description: A report as its page shows it, once opened.

age_seconds.description: Seconds since it was made, when the answer was given.

overdue.description: Older than the time a report is to be reviewed within.

reporter_account_id.description:
Who made it. Every report made now has one; it is absent only for a
report made through an invitation link without signing in, before
reporting needed an account.

OtherAccount.description:
What the other account holds, as the person combining it is shown. Its
address and number are masked; the person proved one of them, and can
sign in to the account and read both anyway.

devices.description: A device of its gets push notifications.

display_name.description: Its name; empty if it has none.

text_updates.description: It has text updates on for at least one agreement.

Part.description: Which stretch of the record a document holds.

complete.description: This one document holds the whole record.

from.description: Where this document starts. Zero and zero for the first.

oneOf.description: Where the next one starts, when the record goes on.

Parties.description:
Each party's name as the agreement writes it: the agreement in force, or
the first proposal until there is one.

PaymentHandleChanges.description:
When each of the payee's payment options changed, as RFC 3339, for those
that changed after the agreement came into force, however long ago: the
payer is warned beside each. A name changed while money is owed is how a
payment is stolen after an account is taken over; one saved before the
agreement is not warned about. Null for the others. Never the old value.

PaymentHandleValue.description:
One payment option to save, as typed: a Venmo username with or without
its `@`, a $Cashtag with or without its `$`, a PayPal.Me name or its
link, or for Zelle an email address or a US phone number.

PaymentHandles.description:
A person's payment options, each optional. In a request, what to save;
in a reply, what is saved, as stored: a Venmo username without its `@`,
a $Cashtag without its `$`, a PayPal.Me name, and for Zelle a lower-case
email address or a US number in international form (`+12025550142`).

cash_app.description:
A Cash App $Cashtag: 1 to 20 letters, digits or `_`, with at least
one letter. A leading `$` is dropped.

paypal.description: A PayPal.Me name: 1 to 20 letters or digits.

venmo.description:
A Venmo username: 5 to 30 letters, digits, `-` or `_`. A leading `@`
is dropped.

zelle.description:
The email address or US phone number Zelle pays this person at.
Shown, never linked: Zelle has no links.

PaymentOptionsShown.description: Whether the signed-in party shows their payment options on an agreement.

PaymentOptionsView.description:
Payment options on one agreement, as one party sees them. Yuppers never
moves money: these open someone else's app, and a payment is recorded
only when the payer says so and the payee confirms it.

shown.description:
Whether the viewer shows their own payment options to the other
party on this agreement.

oneOf.description:
The other party's payment options, only while they show them on
this agreement, it is in force, and the viewer owes them money on it
that is neither marked paid, accepted nor waived. Null otherwise.

theirs_changed.description:
When each of `theirs` changed, for those that changed after the
agreement came into force, however long ago: the payer is warned
beside them to check with the payee another way. Never the old value.
All null when `theirs` is.

Pkpass.description:
A signed Apple pass, a zip archive. Only describes the answer for the
API description; the handler sends the bytes themselves.

channel.description: Which of the account's own identifiers the code was sent to.

code.description: A one-time code sent to it, asked for with `POST /v1/auth/codes`.

amount.description: A positive decimal number such as `2` or `1.5`.

QueuedReport.description:
An open report, as the queue lists it: enough to choose what to open
next, and nothing of what the reporter wrote or who they are. Those are
read by opening the report, which is recorded and limited.

age_seconds.description: Seconds since it was made, when the answer was given.

has_reporter.description:
Whether an account made it. Every report made now has one; it is
false only for a report made through an invitation link without
signing in, before reporting needed an account.

overdue.description: Older than the time a report is to be reviewed within.

RecordContribution.description: Where a contribution of the agreement stands.

since.description: When it came to stand this way. RFC 3339, UTC.

RecordDocument.description:
The record of one exchange, as one self-contained document: a party's
copy to keep or to hand to someone else.

content_hidden.description:
Set when a reviewer has hidden what the parties wrote in this
exchange from the reader (DESIGN.md §9). The terms, the descriptions,
the criteria and every note then read as one placeholder, in
`language`, in this copy, `signed` included, so a fingerprint no longer
matches what is shown. The record itself is unchanged.

contributions.description:
Where each contribution of the agreement stands. These are the
parties' own statements about delivery; the service did not check
them.

history_chain.description:
That the history is chained, and the fingerprint of its last entry,
in the document's language: a printed copy anchors the history with
it (`crate::chain`). Left out while the history has entries from
before the chain that have not been chained yet.

language.description:
The language `notices` and the descriptions are written in. What the
parties wrote is never translated.

prepared_for.description:
Which party this copy was made for. Both parties' copies hold the
same record.

RecordEvent.description:
One entry in the history. The history is append-only: nothing in it is
ever edited or removed, and a correction is a later entry.

by_removed_claimant.description:
Set when the actor was someone who had opened the invitation and was
removed, or left, before the initiator confirmed them. `actor` is
then `B` for the place they were in; they are not the party this
record names as B, and the record does not say who they were.

invitation_named_them.description:
When the invited party joined: whether the invitation named them, so
that no confirmation by the initiator was needed.

note.description:
What the actor wrote with it, exactly as written: the message sent
with a revision, a note on a claim, the reason for a dispute, or a
statement.

oneOf.description: When the exchange closed: how.

The revision the event is about; for an event about a contribution,
the agreement that was in force.

sequence.description: Position in the exchange's history, counting from 1.

signature_void.description:
When whoever opened the invitation was removed or left: whether they
had signed the revision then open, named in `revision`. If so, that
signature is void: it never took effect and never can.

oneOf.description: Where the contribution stood as a result.

statuses.description:
When a revision came into force: where each of its contributions
stood as a result. A contribution of the agreement before that is not
listed was removed by the amendment.

waived.description: When the exchange ended by agreement: what was released, undelivered.

display_code.description: For telling exchanges apart. Not a credential.

oneOf.description: The agreement: in force now, or in force when the exchange closed.

last_event.description: The sequence number of the latest event when this was written.

oneOf.description: The revision waiting to be signed.

timezone.description: The timezone due dates are read in.

RecordRevision.description:
A revision that was sent: what it says, who sent and signed it, and what
became of it.

oneOf.description:
The revision this one answered: the offer it replaced, or the
agreement it proposed to amend.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 of `signed` as canonical JSON (RFC 8785), in hex.

expires_at.description: When it would lapse if not signed by both. RFC 3339, UTC.

note.description: The message sent with it. Not part of what is signed.

oneOf.description:
Only when `signed` is left out: the signed document with every piece
of free text (the terms, and each contribution's description,
completion criteria and unit of quantity) replaced by the placeholder
that says it was hidden by review. Names and amounts are as signed.
It is not what was signed and does not hash to `content_hash`.

sequence.description: 1 for the first proposal, counting up.

signatures.description:
The author's, made by sending it, then the other party's if they
accepted. Only signatures that count are here.

oneOf.description:
What the signatures cover, word for word. Left out when a reviewer
has hidden what was written in the exchange from the reader
(`content_hidden`); `redacted` is there instead.

void_signatures.description:
Signatures that do not count and never will, kept apart so that
nobody reading `signatures` takes one for the other party's.

language.description:
The language the app is showing, as a language tag. Notifications are
written in the account's language, like every email.

token.description: The Expo push token the app was given, `ExponentPushToken[…]`.

RelatedReport.description: Another report about the same exchange.

code.description:
A one-time code sent to the identifier that stays (the account's
other one), asked for with `POST /v1/auth/codes`.

ReportDetail.description:
A report opened for review: what it says, who it is about, the
exchange's record, and what review has done about it so far.

content_hidden.description:
Whether the exchange's content is already hidden from the person
reported.

history.description:
The audit history of this report, its exchange and the person
reported: the latest 200 entries, oldest first.

other_reports.description: The other reports about the same exchange, oldest first.

oneOf.description: The reported exchange's record, with nothing hidden.

ReportReason.description:
Why an exchange is being reported. A fixed list, so that a reviewer can
tell what kind of harm a report is about before reading it.

identifier.description:
An email address, or a phone number: in international form, or a US
number without its country code as people there write it, ten digits
or 1 and ten (`(856) 548-8780`), which is taken as `+1`.

oneOf.description:
For a phone number, required: the box beside it was ticked, with the
version and language of the wording shown. Ignored for an email
address.

channel.description: Which of the account's own identifiers to send the code to.

oneOf.description:
For `PHONE`, required: the box beside the number was ticked, with the
version and language of the wording shown. Ignored for `EMAIL`.

note.description:
What the reviewer found, for the audit history. Required for every
outcome but `DISMISSED`. At most 1,000 characters.

ReviewAction.description: One entry of the audit history.

ReviewEntry.description: One entry of the audit history.

staff_account_id.description:
The reviewer; absent for the owner's command line: naming and
removing reviewers, and a suspension lifted by replaying the deletion
log after a restore, whose note says so.

ReviewOutcome.description: How a reviewer resolved a report.

ReviewQueue.description: The queue of open reports, oldest first.

review_within_hours.description: How soon a report is to be reviewed (DESIGN.md §9).

ReviewRecord.description:
The record of an exchange as a reviewer reads it while a report about
it is open: everything a party's copy holds, for neither party, and with
nothing hidden.

complete.description:
False when the record is longer than one document holds; what is
here is its beginning.

ReviewedAccount.description: One side of a report, as the reviewer is shown it.

merged_into.description:
The account this one was combined into, and when (RFC 3339), if it
was. Its side and name below are that account's, which holds its
place now; acting on this account acts on that one.

name.description: Their name as the exchange writes it; empty if they hold no side.

oneOf.description: Their side of the exchange, if they hold one.

RevisionRef.description: A revision, named both ways: by ID, and by the number people see.

sequence.description: 1 for the first proposal, counting up.

invitation_token.description:
The link token for the invited party, returned once, when the first
revision is sent. Only its hash is kept.

in_force_at.description: When it came into force, if it ever did.

oneOf.description: The revision that took its place, where one did.

since.description: When it came to stand this way. RFC 3339, UTC.

RevisionTerms.description: What a revision says: the part both parties sign.

accepted_by.description:
Who has signed it. The author always has. A signature left by someone
who was removed from the invited party's place is not counted.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 of the signed terms, in hex.

expected_version.description: The exchange version the client last saw.

body.description: The client's working copy, stored as given.

expected_version.description: The exchange version the client last saw.

oneOf.description:
Required when this is the first revision, which also issues the
invitation; ignored after.

note.description: A message to the other party. Not part of what is signed.

oneOf.description: Required to turn them on: the wording shown beside the box.

on.description: `true` to turn updates on, `false` to turn them off.

SignInChannel.description: A kind of identifier a code can be sent to: what someone can sign in with.

Signature.description: One party's signature on one exact revision.

content_hash.description: The hash that was signed, in hex. It is the revision's own.

name.description: The signer's name as that revision writes it.

SignedContribution.description: A contribution as it is signed.

amount_minor.description: Whole minor units of the exchange's currency. Money only.

from.description: The party who owes it; the other receives it.

id.description: The same contribution keeps its ID from one revision to the next.

oneOf.description: Money only.

SignedDocument.description:
Exactly what a signature covers. A revision's content hash is the SHA-256
of this object written as canonical JSON (RFC 8785).

attachments.description: SHA-256 of each attached file, in hex.

timezone.description: The timezone due dates are read in.

Slot.description: One side of the exchange. `A` is the initiator, `B` the invited counterparty.

SmsCodeConsent.description: What the box beside a phone number said, as a client sends it.

language.description: The language it was shown in, as a language tag.

version.description: The version of the wording shown beside the box.

SmsConsent.description: What a party ticked, when turning updates on.

language.description: The language it was shown in, as a language tag.

version.description: The version of the consent wording shown, `consent_version`.

SmsUpdates.description: Where the signed-in party stands on text updates for one agreement.

available.description:
Whether they can be turned on here: text messages are sent, and the
agreement has been sent and is not closed. Turning them off is always
possible.

consent_version.description:
The version of the consent wording a client must show beside the
box, and name when it turns updates on.

on.description:
Whether updates are on for this agreement, to the account's phone
number as it is now.

opted_out.description:
The number replied STOP to our texts, so nothing is texted to it
until it replies START.

phone.description:
The account's phone number, in international form, or null when it
has none; one must be added (`POST /v1/me/identifiers`) first.

StaffNote.description: A reviewer's note, required for lifting a suspension.

Status.description:
Where a contribution stands. Overdue is derived from `Pending` plus the due
condition; it is not a status.

suspended_at.description: When review suspended it, RFC 3339; absent if review did not.

adult_confirmed.description: Only `true` is meaningful: a confirmation cannot be taken back.

dismiss_notice.description: `true` once the account's `notice` has been shown.

language.description:
A language tag. A regional tag falls back to its base language; an
unsupported language is refused.

Verification.description:
The evidence behind a signature: how the signer had shown the service who
they are. It is all the evidence there is.

attribution.description:
The kind of identifier the signer had signed in with, and how long
before signing, in the document's language. Never the address or
number. Left out for a signature made before this was kept.

description.description: The same, in words, in the document's language.

verified_at.description:
When the signer entered that code, which is when they signed in and
can be earlier than the signature. RFC 3339, UTC.

VoidSignature.description:
A signature that never took effect and never can. It was made by someone
who had opened the invitation and was removed, or left, before the
initiator confirmed them. It is kept because it happened. It names
nobody: that person is not the party the revision names.

content_hash.description: The hash that was signed, in hex.

party.description: The place the signer was in.

void_since.description: When the signer was removed or left. RFC 3339, UTC.

WalletLink.description: A link to follow to add a pass.

expires_at.description:
When the link stops working, RFC 3339. Absent for a link that does
not expire.

WalletPlatform.description: A wallet a pass can be added to.

YupCounts.description: How many yups the other account is in, by where they stand.
